page: Vultr vhf-12c-48gb is a High Frequency Compute server configured with 12 shared vCPUs and 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the system features 6 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor configuration includes a 16 MB L3 cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA instructions. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 768 GB NVMe SSD.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mixture of average and top-tier capabilities. The server excels in single-threaded gzip compression, placing in the top 10% of tested systems, and shows strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing performance. Passmark memory testing also ranks in the top 10%. However, memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks (256MB) is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both read and write operations. Standard compute benchmarks, including Geekbench and stress-ng, consistently register in the middle 50% tier.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, this server offers a high-capacity local NVMe storage drive and a substantial memory footprint relative to its shared CPU model. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention tradeoffs, making it less suitable for sustained, heavy multi-core processing. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, text processing, database operations, and lightweight single-threaded compression tasks.
